_note: Saadia-distinctive translation patterns expected to recur in Shemot (Exodus). Unlike data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json, this file does NOT come from a single published study — Blau's published 'Studies in Saadia's Translation' covers only Genesis 1-12. This file is a CURATED CHECKLIST of Saadia's known moves on Shemot, organized by thematic block, to serve as a translation reference. Verify against the Cairo 2019 Tafsir text and Blau's Dictionary of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts (entries cited where relevant).
_status: draft — extend as actual Shemot translations reveal new patterns

expected_patterns.saadia_ja: אלאזלי אלד'י לא יזול (Cairo 3:14) / variants: אלאזלי אלד'י לם יזל, אלאזלי אלאבדי
expected_patterns.en_gloss: the Eternal who never ceases / the Eternal who has never ceased / the Eternal, the Everlasting
expected_patterns.note: Saadia philosophically reframes the divine name as referring to atemporal eternity (אלאזליה). Render the philosophical Arabic, NOT the literal 'I will be what I will be'. The Cairo 2019 reading at Ex 3:14 is 'אלאזלי אלד'י לא יזול' = 'the Eternal who never ceases'.
Saadia's standard 'רב' for אלהי (god of/lord of). Not 'God'.

expected_patterns.he: המקום אשר אתה עומד עליו אדמת-קדש
expected_patterns.en_gloss: a holy place / the consecrated place
expected_patterns.note: Saadia uses מקדס (consecrated) for קדש. Not 'sanctuary' (which would be מקדש in nominal sense).

The Cairo 2019 source uses Saadia's transliteration אלסנא (= the Hebrew סנה). An alternate Saadia recension renders אלעוסג' (ʿawsaj — Arabic boxthorn/lyceum). Either way, the English is 'the thornbush' — not generic 'bush'.
Saadia renders מלאך with the cognate מלאך (angel/messenger), but for יהוה uses אלרב (the Lord).

expected_patterns.en_gloss: Pharaoh's heart was firm / he hardened his heart
expected_patterns.note: Saadia ATTRIBUTES the hardening to Pharaoh (or to natural firmness), softening the divine-causation reading where Hebrew syntax permits. Render literally as the JA, not the Hebrew theological reading.
Saadia uses צ'רב (striking) for מכה (plague/blow).

expected_patterns.en_gloss: a mixture / a mixture of wild beasts
expected_patterns.note: Saadia renders ערב (4th plague) as a mixture/swarm specifically of WILD ANIMALS (סבאע) — choosing the interpretation that ערב means mixed wildlife (vs. mixed insects per LXX). Not 'swarm of flies'.
Saadia's word for דבר (5th plague) is אלמותאן (mortality/murrain).
Saadia's medical term for the 6th plague (boils with blistering).
Direct cognate — keep 'hail'.
Saadia intensifies — 'darkness of murkiness'. Render with intensifier.
Saadia transliterates rather than translates. Keep 'Passover'.
Saadia's standard word for מצות. Don't use 'matzot' — render with the descriptive English.

expected_patterns.en_gloss: the people of Egypt / the Egyptians

expected_patterns.note: Saadia identifies ים סוף with بحر القلزم (Qulzum, the medieval Arabic name for the Red Sea, near Suez). On first occurrence: 'the Sea of Qulzum (Red Sea)'. Thereafter: 'the Sea of Qulzum'.

expected_patterns.he: ירד / וירד יהוה על הר סיני
expected_patterns.saadia_ja: צ'הר נור אללה / אט'הר אללה נורה
expected_patterns.en_gloss: the light of God appeared / God manifested His light
expected_patterns.note: Saadia's signature anti-anthropomorphic move: God doesn't 'descend' — His LIGHT (or majesty) appears. Same pattern as Bereshit ויעל אלהים → 'the light of God ascended'. KEEP THE LIGHT METAPHOR.
Saadia softens by removing the literal 'faces'.

expected_patterns.he: ויאמר אלהים את כל הדברים האלה (Ex 20:1)
expected_patterns.note: Saadia uses כלם (speech-act, not vocal speech) for the Decalogue speech — preserves direct divine speech but with abstract speech-act verb.

expected_patterns.he: לא תרצח / לא תנאף / לא תגנב
expected_patterns.saadia_ja: לא תקתל / לא תזן / לא תסרק
expected_patterns.en_gloss: you shall not kill / you shall not commit adultery / you shall not steal
expected_patterns.note: Direct cognate triplet.
Saadia uses שביה (= classical shabīh, 'similar form') for תמונה — preserves the anti-anthropomorphic edge: don't worship a 'form'.
Direct cognate — keep 'tabernacle' (the standard English term for the desert sanctuary).

expected_patterns.en_gloss: the ark of the testimony / the ark of the covenant
expected_patterns.note: Saadia uses תאבות (tābūt, the Arabic word for ark/chest) — same cognate field as Qur'ānic Arabic.
Saadia renders the 'mercy seat' (Christian term) literally as a 'cover/lid' — without atonement-theology overlay.
Saadia transliterates.
Saadia transliterates.
Saadia transliterates without translation (terms whose precise meaning was uncertain by his era).
Saadia uses Persian-derived terms for the dyes. אסמאנגוני (sky-colored) for תכלת is the standard Saadia rendering.
Per Blau (on Gen 3:1, 18:21): Saadia uses אד' for 'since/when' (temporal/causal) and אן for 'if' (conditional). In legal contexts, אד'א opens case-protasis ('if/when X occurs').

expected_patterns.saadia_ja: ערץ' עין מקאן עין / קימה' עין
expected_patterns.en_gloss: the value of an eye in place of an eye / compensation for an eye
expected_patterns.note: Saadia's signature legal move: 'eye for eye' is MONETARY COMPENSATION, not literal mutilation. This is the standard Talmudic reading rendered into the translation. Keep the compensation framing.
Direct cognate.

blocks.block: general Saadia moves likely in Shemot

expected_patterns.note: Saadia consistently uses קאל ל (vs. classical אמר ל).

expected_patterns.en_gloss: the power of God / the might of God
expected_patterns.note: Saadia's anti-anthropomorphic move: 'hand of God' → 'power of God'. Same pattern as in Genesis.
Saadia uses Arabic forms of biblical names: מוסי (Moses), הארון (Aaron), יוסף (Joseph), אבראהים (Abraham). Render with the standard English biblical names.
